THE PERSIANS
934-1629 CE
IRANIAN DYNASTIES, DIVANS, TRADE
Difficulty: 3 stars

The collapse of the Sassanian Empire saw Persia fall into disunity for over 700 years. Yet, in spite of its fractionalization, Persian culture, language, and martial traditions continued to foster and grow. In Age of Empires IV, the Persian civilization represents the various medieval dynasties, both native and foreign, that ruled over the region of “Ērān.” In-game, Persia sports a powerful economy, with an emphasis on trade and flexibility. In combat, this is THE “counter” civ, with units that are weaker at a base level, but much more effective against their counters.

STRENGTHS:
Strong economy enabled by Divans that can supervise.
Flexible - can easily switch army compositions.
Very strong trade!
Zamburak Siege Camels!

WEAKNESSES:
Cannot upgrade unit Veterancy seperately.
Units are weak in general-purpose roles.
Weak in early Imperial due to expensive techs.

UNIQUE UNITS:
Qizilbash: Fast moving Horse Archer that deals bonus damage to melee units.
Daylamite: Cheap Man-at-arms with less armor, but deals bonus damage to light infantry.
Savar: Slow, tanky Lancer with an anti-armor mace attack.
Assassin*: Stealthed killer that first strikes for double damage. Can’t attack buildings but can Sabotage them.
Zamburak*: Siege Camelry. Functions like Mounted Ozutsu. Place it in the Archery Range just like the Grenadier.

IRANIAN DYNASTIES:
Medieval Iran was a melting pot of diverse cultures and transient empires. Each conquering dynasty brought their own veteran forces with them. This is represented in-game by the Dynasty system.

Unlike other civilization’s units, Persian units do not research veterancy individually. Instead, all of your units are upgraded simultaneously as you upgrade your dynasty.

Buyid (Regular) ➟ Khwarazmid (Hardened) ➟ Il-Khanid (Veteran) ➟ Safavid (Elite)

MILITARY SPECIALIZATION:
All of Persia’s unique units have less base damage but more bonus damage vs. the units they counter. This makes them weaker as generalist units but much stronger as specialist units.

INFLUENCE - DYNASTIC BUREAUCRACY:
Each time you advance your Dynasty, you can build an additional Divan. Divans are special buildings that can supervise nearby structures (think Chinese Imperial Official, but in the form of a building). Choose either:

Divan of Commerce:
Houses unique economic technologies. Emits an aura range of 4 units.
Ability: Commerce Vizier - Supervise a nearby economic drop-off, granting +20% bonus resources and improving research speed (does not affect Town Centers, Docks, or Markets).

Divan of War:
Houses unique military technologies. Emits an influence range of 4 units.
Ability: War Vizier - Supervise a military production or technology building within the Divan’s influence, boosting its military production or research speed by +150%.

UNIQUE BUILDING: CARAVANSERAI:
Unique structure that massively buffs nearby Traders’ movement speed and armor. Unlocked in the Castle Age.

TURKOMAN HORSE ARCHERS:
In the Feudal Age unlock the Qizilbash, a unique Horse Archer that counters melee units. In Age IV, research Turkoman Traditions to enable the Qizilbash to attack while moving, just like Mongol Mangudai.

GARDEN BOUNTY:
Mills constructed near Berry Bushes create Orchards, increasing Food capacity by +100. Gather from Berry Bushes +30% faster, but cannot gather from Boar. Berry carry capacity increased +3.

We cannot affect unit visuals, building visuals, voice lines, sound effects, music, or image assets, so all assets are recycled.

THE KOREANS
918-1598 CE
ARCHERY, DEFENSE, TECHNOLOGY
Difficulty Rating: **
DESCRIPTION:
Known as a “land of fortresses”, Korea under the Joseon Dynasty has had to endure countless invasions both the Mongols/Chinese on their northern frontier and from the Japanese along their southern coast. In game, they are a defensive-focused civilization that uses a unique resource called “Literature” to fuel their research advantage. On the field, their powerful, long-range archers and advanced rocket artillery enable them to make the first strike in any engagement they choose to take.
Unique Units:
Seonbi Scholar: Economic unit that can supervise buildings.
Tiger Hunter: Slow-moving armored Archer.
Gapsa: Armored Spearman, anti-cav specialist.
Hwacha: Nest-of-bees but as indirect artillery.
Hwarang: Flower Knights that switch stances between horse archer and man-at-arms.
Righteous Army Monk: Warrior Monk that doesn’t cost pop space but also can’t be controlled.
Turtle Ship: Tanky ship with a short-range Hwacha ability.
Unique Resource - Literature
Korea has a unique 5th resource called Literature (문), which represents the creation of scientific and cultural works. All Korean technologies ONLY cost Literature.
Unique Building - Seowon Academy
A Confucian academy that passively generates Literature based on the amount of natural resources nearby (Limit 8).
Influence - Natural Defenses
Seowons generate additional Literature for each Outpost (+3) and Mountain Fortress (+10) placed within their influence. Other Seowons can’t be built in the same area.
Unique Unit - Seonbi Scholar
Seonbi are Confucian scholars trained from the Seowon. They can supervise Seowon Academies to boost Literature generation by +25%. Multiple Seonbi Scholars can supervise the same Seowon Academy, stacking their boosts.
Like Imperial Officials, the Seonbi Scholar can also supervise buildings to improve research/production speed by 150%. Unlike Imperial Officials, Seonbi do not collect taxes, and do not boost resource efficiency when supervising a drop-off.
Foreign Exchange
The Seowon Academy can also access unique techs from other civilizations. Each game, 4 random foreign techs are made available, and the player can choose 2 of them to research.
All players can see what foreign techs are available to Korea at anytime by using a special info button in their Town Center.
Literature can also be exchanged for resources at the Market.
Tiger Hunter Corps
The chakhogapsa were an elite corps of Tiger Hunters recruited for their bravery. These armored archers are available starting in Age 2, and function like ranged Men-at-arms.
Land of Mountain Fortresses
The Mountain Fortress (Sanseong) is a special Keep that comes equipped with a Hwacha rocket artillery ability.
Water Bonus - Haenyeo divers
Fishing boats passively generate Literature. This can be upgraded to also allow military ships to generate Literature.
Strengths:
Unique 5th resource “Literature” used for techs.
Can research techs from other civilizations.
Powerful Archers.
Strong defenses, including Hwacha rocket launchers.
Strong armored units.
Weaknesses:
No economic bonuses aside from Literature.
Weak tempo.
Gold hungry units.
Units require a lot of micro.
Vulnerable to raiding in the early game.
Immobile army.
